samples: As a retired researcher running small behavioral-economics experiments and lightweight web apps, the Developer plan hits the only viable sweet spot. Beginner's restricted outbound Internet access kills any API or live-data work immediately — unacceptable. Custom is absurd overkill for a single person tinkering in retirement. Developer gives one real web app, 5,000 CPU-seconds/day, 5 GB disk, unrestricted Internet, and a 30-day money-back guarantee that fully satisfies my risk-averse temperament. $10/month is a negligible cost for a middle-income retiree who values novelty and wants a clean, hosted environment without the friction of self-managed infrastructure.

As a premium-seeking student running small personal Python projects and a lightweight web app, the Developer plan delivers exactly the right configuration: one web app with a custom domain, SSH access, full unrestricted outbound internet, 5,000 CPU-seconds per day, IPython/Jupyter notebook support, and 5GB of disk space — all at a fixed $10/month. The Beginner plan is disqualifying: restricted outbound internet breaks real experiments, only 100 CPU-seconds per day is insufficient, no SSH, and no scheduled tasks. The Custom plan is architectural overkill for a solo student with one project at a time. Developer hits the premium-but-practical sweet spot this persona demands.
